Note::TexAccessor::frac_slash¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::frac_slash() const

Rewrite Fraction Commands As Explicit Division¶

frac_slash() rewrites complete \frac, \dfrac, \tfrac, and \cfrac calls from \frac{numerator}{denominator} to (numerator)/(denominator). Parentheses are always inserted around both operands. They preserve the fraction’s grouping when the result is embedded in a larger expression; the method does not guess whether either pair is stylistically dispensable.

Both required groups must be balanced before a call is converted. Nested braces are understood, and nested supported fraction commands are converted recursively from the inside of each operand. Whitespace between the control word and its groups is accepted; leading and trailing ASCII whitespace inside each operand is removed. Other content inside an operand is retained exactly.

This is a source rewrite, not symbolic algebra. It does not evaluate numbers, cancel factors, distribute division, convert roots, or remove math delimiters. Likewise, a similarly prefixed command such as \fraction is unrelated and remains unchanged. A command following the linebreak control symbol \\ is also left alone, and incomplete calls are preserved rather than partially destroyed. Those boundaries make the operation safe for preprocessing mixed TeX source where only complete fraction constructs should change.

The output is a newly allocated Text Note with the receiver’s exact rank and shape. Empty cells remain empty and cells without a convertible call are copied unchanged. Undefined input remains undefined. Bool, Int64, Float64, and Bytes Notes reject because their lanes are not TeX source. Runtime is linear in ordinary source length, with additional traversal proportional to nested fraction content; the receiver is never mutated.

Example 1: The Four Fraction Spellings¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    R"(\frac{1}{2} + \dfrac{a+b}{c} + \tfrac{m}{n} + \cfrac{p}{q})");
std::cout << source.tex().frac_slash() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"(1)/(2) + (a+b)/(c) + (m)/(n) + (p)/(q)"

Example 2: Nested Fractions¶

const auto fractions = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\frac{1}{2} + \dfrac{a+b}{c} + \cfrac{\frac{x}{y}}{z})",
    R"(\fraction{1}{2} + \\frac{3}{4} + \frac{broken})"});

std::cout << fractions.tex().frac_slash() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["(1)/(2) + (a+b)/(c) + ((x)/(y))/(z)", "\\fraction{1}{2} + \\\\frac{3}{4} + \\frac{broken}"]

The nested numerator is recursively rewritten. The second lane demonstrates all three preservation boundaries: a different command name, a linebreak, and an incomplete second argument.

Example 3: Higher-Rank Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\frac{a}{b})", "plain",
                             R"(\tfrac{x}{y})", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().frac_slash() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["(a)/(b)", "plain"], 
  ["(x)/(y)", ""]
]

Example 4: Undefined Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().frac_slash().defined()
          << '\n';

Output¶

false

Example 5: Non-Text Input Rejects¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().frac_slash();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "fractions Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

fractions Int64: rejected
